verses.zh: 耶和华对挪亚说：「你和你的全家都要进入方舟；因为在这世代中，我见你在我面前是义人。
verses.en: The Lord said to Noah, “Come into the ark, you and all your household, for I consider you godly among this generation.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for you I see [as] godly before me in this generation.” The direct object (“you”) is placed first in the clause to give it prominence. The verb “to see” here signifies God’s evaluative discernment.

verses.zh: 凡洁净的畜类，你要带七公七母；不洁净的畜类，你要带一公一母；
verses.en: You must take with you seven pairs[NOTE:1] of every kind of clean animal,[NOTE:2] the male and its mate,[NOTE:3] two of every kind of unclean animal, the male and its mate,
notes: Or “seven” (cf. NIV84). Since seven is an odd number, and “seven” is qualified as male and female, only seven pairs can match the description (cf. NIV11, NRSV, HCSB).
For a study of the Levitical terminology of “clean” and “unclean,” see L. E. Toombs, IDB 1:643.
Heb “a male and his female” (also a second time at the end of this verse). The terms used here for male and female animals (אִישׁ, ʾish and אִשָּׁה, ʾishah) normally refer to humans.

verses.zh: 空中的飞鸟也要带七公七母，可以留种，活在全地上；
verses.en: and also seven pairs[NOTE:1] of every kind of bird in the sky, male and female,[NOTE:2] to preserve their offspring[NOTE:3] on the face of the entire earth.
notes: Or “seven” (cf. NIV84).
Here (and in v. 9) the Hebrew text uses the normal generic terms for “male and female” (זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, zakhar uneqevah).
Heb “to keep alive offspring.”

verses.zh: 因为再过七天，我要降雨在地上四十昼夜，把我所造的各种活物都从地上除灭。」
verses.en: For in seven days[NOTE:1] I will cause it to rain[NOTE:2] on the earth for 40 days and 40 nights, and I will wipe from the face of the ground every living thing that I have made.”
notes: Heb “for seven days yet,” meaning “after [or “in”] seven days.”
The Hiphil participle מַמְטִיר (mamtir, “cause to rain”) here expresses the certainty of the act in the imminent future.

verses.zh: 挪亚就遵着耶和华所吩咐的行了。
verses.en: And Noah did all[NOTE:1] that the Lord commanded him.
notes: Heb “according to all.”

verses.zh: 当洪水泛滥在地上的时候，挪亚整六百岁。
verses.en: Noah[NOTE:1] was 600 years old when the floodwaters engulfed[NOTE:2] the earth.
notes: Heb “Now Noah was.” The disjunctive clause (conjunction plus subject plus predicate nominative after implied “to be” verb) provides background information. The age of Noah receives prominence.

Heb “and the flood was water upon.” The disjunctive clause (conjunction plus subject plus verb) is circumstantial/temporal in relation to the preceding clause. The verb הָיָה (hayah) here carries the nuance “to come” (BDB 225 s.v. הָיָה). In this context the phrase “come upon” means “to engulf.”

verses.zh: 挪亚就同他的妻和儿子儿妇都进入方舟，躲避洪水。
verses.en: Noah entered the ark along with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives because of[NOTE:1] the floodwaters.
notes: The preposition מִן (min) is causal here, explaining why Noah and his family entered the ark.

verses.zh: 洁净的畜类和不洁净的畜类，飞鸟并地上一切的昆虫，
verses.en: Pairs[NOTE:1] of clean animals, of unclean animals, of birds, and of everything that creeps along the ground,
notes: Heb “two two” meaning “in twos.”

verses.zh: 都是一对一对地，有公有母，到挪亚那里进入方舟，正如　神所吩咐挪亚的。
verses.en: male and female, came into the ark to Noah,[NOTE:1] just as God had commanded him.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text of vv. 8-9a reads, “From the clean animal[s] and from the animal[s] which are not clean and from the bird[s] and everything that creeps on the ground, two two they came to Noah to the ark, male and female.”
Heb “Noah”; the pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 过了那七天，洪水泛滥在地上。
verses.en: And after seven days the floodwaters engulfed the earth.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “came upon.”

verses.zh: 当挪亚六百岁，二月十七日那一天，大渊的泉源都裂开了，天上的窗户也敞开了，
verses.en: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month—on that day all the fountains of the great deep[NOTE:1] burst open and the floodgates of the heavens[NOTE:2] were opened.
notes: The watery deep. The same Hebrew term used to describe the watery deep in Gen 1:2 (תְּהוֹם, tehom) appears here. The text seems to picture here subterranean waters coming from under the earth and contributing to the rapid rise of water. The significance seems to be, among other things, that in this judgment God was returning the world to its earlier condition of being enveloped with water—a judgment involving the reversal of creation. On Gen 7:11 see G. F. Hasel, “The Fountains of the Great Deep,” Origins 1 (1974): 67-72; idem, “The Biblical View of the Extent of the Flood,” Origins 2 (1975): 77-95.tn The Hebrew term תְּהוֹם (tehom, “deep”) refers to the watery deep, the salty ocean—especially the primeval ocean that surrounds and underlies the earth (see Gen 1:2).
On the prescientific view of the sky reflected here, see L. I. J. Stadelmann, The Hebrew Conception of the World (AnBib), 46.

verses.zh: 四十昼夜降大雨在地上。
verses.en: And the rain fell[NOTE:1] on the earth 40 days and 40 nights.
notes: Heb “was.”

verses.zh: 正当那日，挪亚和他三个儿子闪、含、雅弗，并挪亚的妻子和三个儿妇，都进入方舟。
verses.en: On that very day Noah entered the ark, accompanied by his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, along with his wife and his sons’ three wives.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “On that very day Noah entered, and Shem and Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and the wife of Noah, and the three wives of his sons with him into the ark.”

verses.zh: 他们和百兽，各从其类，一切牲畜，各从其类，爬在地上的昆虫，各从其类，一切禽鸟，各从其类，都进入方舟。
verses.en: They entered,[NOTE:1] along with every living creature after its kind, every animal after its kind, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, everything with wings.[NOTE:2]
notes: The verb “entered” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “every bird, every wing.”

verses.zh: 凡有血肉、有气息的活物，都一对一对地到挪亚那里，进入方舟。
verses.en: Pairs[NOTE:1] of all creatures[NOTE:2] that have the breath of life came into the ark to Noah.
notes: Heb “two two” meaning “in twos.”
Heb “flesh.”

verses.zh: 凡有血肉进入方舟的，都是有公有母，正如　神所吩咐挪亚的。耶和华就把他关在方舟里头。
verses.en: Those that entered were male and female,[NOTE:1] just as God commanded him. Then the Lord shut him in.
notes: Heb “Those that went in, male and female from all flesh they went in.”

verses.zh: 洪水泛滥在地上四十天，水往上长，把方舟从地上漂起。
verses.en: The flood engulfed the earth for 40 days. As the waters increased, they lifted the ark and raised it above the earth.

verses.zh: 水势浩大，在地上大大地往上长，方舟在水面上漂来漂去。
verses.en: The waters completely overwhelmed[NOTE:1] the earth, and the ark floated[NOTE:2] on the surface of the waters.
notes: Heb “and the waters were great and multiplied exceedingly.” The first verb in the sequence is וַיִּגְבְּרוּ (vayyigberu, from גָּבַר, gavar), meaning “to become great, mighty.” The waters did not merely rise; they “prevailed” over the earth, overwhelming it.
Heb “went.”

verses.zh: 水势在地上极其浩大，天下的高山都淹没了。
verses.en: The waters completely inundated[NOTE:1] the earth so that even[NOTE:2] all the high mountains under the entire sky were covered.
notes: Heb “and the waters were great exceedingly, exceedingly.” The repetition emphasizes the depth of the waters.
Heb “and.”

verses.zh: 水势比山高过十五肘，山岭都淹没了。
verses.en: The waters rose more than 20 feet[NOTE:1] above the mountains.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “rose 15 cubits.” Since a cubit is considered by most authorities to be about 18 inches, this would make the depth 22.5 feet. This figure might give the modern reader a false impression of exactness, however, so in the translation the phrase “15 cubits” has been rendered “more than 20 feet.”

Heb “the waters prevailed 15 cubits upward and they covered the mountains.” Obviously, a flood of 20 feet did not cover the mountains; the statement must mean the flood rose about 20 feet above the highest mountain.

verses.zh: 凡在地上有血肉的动物，就是飞鸟、牲畜、走兽，和爬在地上的昆虫，以及所有的人，都死了。
verses.en: And all living things[NOTE:1] that moved on the earth died, including the birds, domestic animals, wild animals, all the creatures that swarm over the earth, and all humankind.
notes: Heb “flesh.”

verses.zh: 凡在旱地上、鼻孔有气息的生灵都死了。
verses.en: Everything on dry land that had the breath[NOTE:1] of life in its nostrils died.
notes: The MT reads נִשְׁמַת רוּחַ חַיִּים (nishmat ruakh khayyim, “breath of the breath/spirit of life”), but the LXX and Vulgate imply only נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים (nishmat khayyim). Either the LXX translator omitted translation of both words because of their similarity in meaning, or the omission in LXX shows that the inclusion of רוּחַ in the MT is the addition of an explanatory gloss.

verses.zh: 凡地上各类的活物，连人带牲畜、昆虫，以及空中的飞鸟，都从地上除灭了，只留下挪亚和那些与他同在方舟里的。
verses.en: So the Lord[NOTE:1] destroyed[NOTE:2] every living thing that was on the surface of the ground, including people, animals, creatures that creep along the ground, and birds of the sky.[NOTE:3] They were wiped off the earth. Only Noah and those who were with him in the ark survived.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “wiped away” (cf. NRSV “blotted out”).
Heb “from man to animal to creeping thing and to the bird of the sky.”

The Hebrew verb שָׁאָר (shaʾar) means “to be left over; to survive” in the Niphal verb stem. It is the word used in later biblical texts for the remnant that escapes judgment. See G. F. Hasel, “Semantic Values of Derivatives of the Hebrew Root šʾr,” AUSS 11 (1973): 152-69.

verses.zh: 水势浩大，在地上共一百五十天。
verses.en: The waters prevailed over[NOTE:1] the earth for 150 days.
notes: The Hebrew verb translated “prevailed over” suggests that the waters were stronger than the earth. The earth and everything in it were no match for the return of the chaotic deep.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible
Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 7:1-5

1Then the Lord said to Noah, "Enter the ark, you and all your household, for you alone I have seen to be righteous before Me in this time. 2You shall take with you of every clean animal by sevens, a male and his female; and of the animals that are not clean two, a male and his female; 3also of the birds of the sky, by sevens, male and female, to keep offspring alive on the face of all the earth. 4For after seven more days, I will send rain on the earth forty days and forty nights; and I will blot out from the face of the land every living thing that I have made." 5Noah did according to all that the Lord had commanded him.

7:1 "the Lord said to Noah" This is the covenant name for
Israel's Deity, YHWH, here but in Gen. 7:16 He is called Elohim. The rabbinical understanding
of these names referring to God are aspects of His character; savior (YHWH) and Creator (Elohim).
This seems to fit the usages of the Pentateuch.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR
DEITY, C. and D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PENTATEUCH SOURCE CRITICISM

▣ "Enter the ark" This VERB (BDB 92, KB 112) is a Qal
IMPERATIVE. The timing is at YHWH's descretion.

Just a word to remind you of the ambiguous construction terms related to the
ark, the tabernacle, and David/Solomon's temple. Moderns simply cannot reconstruct these things based
on the discriptions in the Bible.

▣ "for you alone I have seen to be righteous before Me in this time" The term
"righteous" here is used in the same sense as referring to Job as "blameless" (cf, Gen. 6:9). This does not imply a
sinlessness but one who has conformed to and performed all that they understand or is culturally expressed
in relation to God.

Notice that Noah's righteousness affects his family. This is a biblical truth. This does not
mean that someone can be right with God based on another person's merit, but it does imply that spiritual
blessings flow from those who know God to those with whom they are acquainted and with whom they are
intimately involved (compare Deut. 5:9-10; 7:9 and 1 Cor. 7:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOUSEHOLD BAPTISMS

7:2 "clean animal by sevens, a male and his female" There is a distinction between clean and unclean.
However, nothing is said about the criteria. Later in the life of the nation of Israel, YHWH will reveal the
distinction. In this period of Israel's history, the unclean animals were often related to the surrounding
pagan cultures. The food laws of Leviticus 11 were one way to separate Israel from the nations. I see the
food laws as religious, not hygienic (see notes online at Leviticus 11). In Gen. 9:3 all animals are allowed
for food, but in Gen. 5:20 only "clean" animals were sacrificed to God.

There has been much discussion about "by seven." Literally "seven, seven." It is translated
"seven pairs" in NRSV, NJB, JPSOA. Does it mean seven individual animals or seven pairs of animals? The
phrase "male and his female" implies pairs.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT FOOD LAWS

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC
NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4

7:4 "seven more days, I will send rain on the earth" Rashi says that this was the period of mourning
for the righteous Methuselah who had just died. The rabbinical Midrash believed that God did not send the
flood until Methuselah passed away.

The origin of the week is shrouded in mystery. The best option is not related to the solar
or lunar cycles, but to the recurrent use of "seven" in the Gilgamesh Epic and the Ba'al poetry of
Ugarit. see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 186-188.

▣ "forty days and forty nights" The term "forty" is used quite often in the Bible (see a
concordance). At times it is meant to be taken literally but at other times it simply means a long period
of indefinite time (longer than a lunar cycle which is twenty-eight and one-half days, but shorter than a
seasonal change). In several Mesopotamian accounts the time frame of the flood is seven days.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC
NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

7:5 Noah's righteousness is connected to his obedience (cf. Gen. 6:22; 7:5,9,16).

The VERB "commanded" (BDB 845, KB 1010, Piel PERFECT)
must relate to special revelation from YHWH (i.e., "YHWH said to Noah," v. 1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 7:6-12

6Now Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of water came upon the earth. 7Then Noah and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him entered the ark because of the water of the flood. 8Of clean animals and animals that are not clean and birds and everything that creeps on the ground, 9there went into the ark to Noah by twos, male and female, as God had commanded Noah. 10It came about after the seven days, that the water of the flood came upon the earth. 11In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on the same day all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the floodgates of the sky were opened. 12The rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.

7:11 "all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the floodgates of the sky were opened" The
dating of Gen. 7:11 is very specific in this verse (which implies a historical event) as well as the
VERBS which describe the physical catastrophe that occurred on the earth (two Niphal
PERFECTS, BDB 131, KB 149 and BDB 834, KB 986). We can see the scale of destruction in
Gen. 7:18 and 19 in the Hebrew text. Many of the earth's physical features may have been changed especially
in the Near East.

There are two sources of the water:

- fountains of the deep (cf. Gen. 1:9)

- foodgates (i.e., windows, cf. Ps. 78:23ff; Mal. 3:10) of the sky (i.e., the waters above, Gen. 1:6-8)

This is an obvious reversal of what God did in Gen. 1:6-10. Watery chaos returns.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WINDOWS OF HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 7:13-16

13On the very same day Noah and Shem and Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah's wife and the three wives of his sons with them, entered the ark, 14they and every beast after its kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, all sorts of birds. 15So they went into the ark to Noah, by twos of all flesh in which was the breath of life. 16Those that entered, male and female of all flesh, entered as God had commanded him; and the Lord closed it behind him.

7:13 "On the very same day" This is a Hebrew idiom, "bone of the day." This NOUN root
"bone" (BDB 782, #3, KB 869, #4) is used in this sense several times (cf. Gen. 17:23,26; Exod. 12:17,41,51;
Lev. 23:14,21,28,29,30; Deut. 32:48; Josh. 5:11; 10:27; Ezek. 24:2; 40:1).

7:14 This includes all the categories of land animals mentioned in Genesis 1, excluding the sea life.

7:16 "and the Lord closed it behind him" YHWH closed the door
Himself (see note Gen. 3:8; 8:21; 11:5). The rabbinical Midrash says that He did this in order to keep
the wicked out of the ark. They even go so far as to assert that God surrounded the ark with lions and
bears to keep the people away.

To me, the ark is another act of YHWH's mercy to mankind to continue the
Messianic line, even amidst judgment, which would eventually provide redemption (cf. Gen. 3:15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD
DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL
REDEMPTIVE PLAN

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 7:17-24

17Then the flood came upon the earth for forty days, and the water increased and lifted up the ark, so that it rose above the earth. 18The water prevailed and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the water. 19The water prevailed more and more upon the earth, so that all the high mountains everywhere under the heavens were covered. 20The water prevailed fifteen cubits higher, and the mountains were covered. 21All flesh that moved on the earth perished, birds and cattle and beasts and every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth, and all mankind; 22of all that was on the dry land, all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, died. 23Thus He blotted out every living thing that was upon the face of the land, from man to animals to creeping things and to birds of the sky, and they were blotted out from the earth; and only Noah was left, together with those that were with him in the ark. 24The water prevailed upon the earth one hundred and fifty days.

7:19 The language of this verse certainly implies a worldwide flood (cf. Gen. 8:21; 2 Pet. 3:6). But
does it? The term "earth" (erets, BDB 75, can mean "land" (cf. Gen. 41:57). It may be a hyperbolic idiom
similar to Luke 2:1 and Col. 1:23 (cf. Hard Sayings of the Bible, IVP pp. 112-114). As for the
theology of the flood, its extent is irrelevant. There is not a consistent flood deposit even in Mesopotamia
much less the whole world! Floods were common in Mesopotamia because of the two large river systems that
combine at their mouths. A book that has been very helpful to me in this area is Bernard Ramm, The
Christian's View of Science and Scripture, pp. 156-178.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND,
COUNTRY, EARTH

"prevailed more and more"

NKJV, Peshitta
"prevailed exceedingly"

NRSV
"swelled so mightly"

TEV
"became so deep"

NJB
"rose higher and higher"

JPSOA
"swelled much more"

REB
"increased more and more"

LXX
"prevailing very greatly"

There is a series of phrases that express the rising flood waters.

- Gen. 7:19 ‒ "the water increased"

- Gen. 7:17 ‒ "it rose above the earth"

- Gen. 7:18 ‒ "the water prevailed and increased greatly"

- Gen. 7:19 ‒ "the water prevailed more and more"

- Gen. 7:19 ‒ "all the high mountaiins everywhere under the heavens were covered"

- Gen. 7:20 ‒ "the waters prevailed fifteen cubits higher, and the mountinas were covered"

Verses 18 and 19 use the ADVERB "greatly" (BDB 547). Verse 19 doubles it for emphasis.
The question of the extent of the flood is linked to the dispersion of the animals and mankind from Eden.

7:20 "cubits" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CUBIT

7:22 "the breath of the spirit of life" Apparently the aquatic life was spared, but all other air-breathing life was
destroyed. There is a purposeful distinction between animals that have the breath of life and mankind who has the breath
of God (Gen. 2:7; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 133). Six humans will be spared and start the new humanity. Originally all humans
were "children of Adam," but now all humans will be "children of Noah."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is your understanding of the phrase "the sons of God" and why?

- Why do you think that angels would want to take human women?

- Who were the Nephilim?

- How could God repent?

- What does it mean to walk with God?

- Why weren't the fish judged along with the land animals?

- What is a clean and unclean animal in Noah's setting?

- Was the flood local or universal? Why?
